transformations.rationale: The Rust method receiver `self` is represented as the explicit Verus parameter `slice`; the public target remains executable and carries the generated permutation plus key-sorted contract.

The Rust 1.96 body passes `&mut |a, b| f(a).lt(&f(b))` to `sort::unstable::sort`. This Verus build cannot typecheck that mutable FnMut key closure directly, so the harness lowers only that closure adapter to a named key-observation boundary while preserving the key extraction, Ord::lt comparison intent, and source-backed unstable-sort call.

The recursive private unstable-sort implementation behind `sort::unstable::sort` is isolated as a named source-backed helper boundary. The public target function is executable and not `external_body`.
